scope: Phase 4 and Phase 5 runtime texture assets
transform_policy: Four source-image assets are byte-for-byte official NASA or USGS downloads with local renames only. Earth's runtime albedo and night map are documented 8192 × 4096 WebP reductions of official NASA global maps, and its 8192 × 4096 cloud map is a documented WebP encoding of NASA's official TIFF. Six PNG material maps and three lossless WebPs are deterministic project-generated derivatives. Mercury, Moon, and Mars normals come from quantitative elevation rasters; the three Earth material maps are visual heuristics derived from the bundled 8192 × 4096 Blue Marble runtime image and are not measured geophysical products. Phase 5 derives its Jupiter runtime map without resizing or recoloring from the official Hubble OPAL Cycle 32 Rotation A TIFF, adds a disclosed mixed-date grayscale detail residual derived from NASA PIA23606, and derives a coverage-aware Saturn map from the official Hubble OPAL Cycle 32 Rotation A TIFF; all jet, storm, and ring profiles are code/data inputs rather than raster assets.

source.organization: U.S. Geological Survey Astrogeology Science Center; MESSENGER source observations from NASA and mission partners
source.title: Mercury MESSENGER USGS DEM Global 665m v2
source.data_semantics: Single-band quantitative elevation in metres relative to the 2,439,400 m Mercury datum radius; equirectangular, planetocentric, positive-east, 0 to 360 degrees longitude.

transforms: Decode the single-band GeoTIFF as quantitative height and resize to 2048 x 1024 with Lanczos3 filtering.
Roll the resampled raster by 180 degrees (half its width) so the source 0 to 360 degree longitude domain aligns with the runtime -180 to 180 degree color map.
Compute central height differences with longitude wrap, clamped polar rows, and latitude-aware east-west metre spacing using a 2,439,400 m radius.
Multiply physical surface slopes by 36 for visual legibility, normalize the tangent-space vector, encode XYZ from [-1, 1] to RGB [0, 255], and write a compressed PNG. The sphere is not displaced.

assets.license_note: USGS-produced content is generally in the U.S. public domain; the product record requests citation of its authors. The normal map is a project-generated derivative. Credit USGS Astrogeology and the MESSENGER mission originators; attribution does not imply endorsement.

channel.semantics: Project-generated shading normals derived from quantitative USGS elevation. Slope is visually amplified 36x; values are not elevation, do not displace geometry, and are not unmodified USGS data.

source.organization: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center Scientific Visualization Studio; Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Laser Altimeter team
source.title: CGI Moon Kit LOLA displacement map, 16 pixels per degree, unsigned 16-bit
source.data_semantics: Unsigned 16-bit LOLA displacement samples at 0.5 m per digital number. NASA's unsigned product adds a constant 20,000-DN offset to the signed half-metre heights relative to a 1,737,400 m radius; that constant cancels in normal-map gradients. The map is centered at 0 degrees longitude.

transforms: Decode the unsigned single-band TIFF, convert height differences at 0.5 m per digital number, and resize to 2048 x 1024 with Lanczos3 filtering.
Compute central height differences with longitude wrap, clamped polar rows, and latitude-aware east-west metre spacing using a 1,737,400 m radius; no longitude roll is applied.
Multiply physical surface slopes by 48 for visual legibility, normalize the tangent-space vector, encode XYZ from [-1, 1] to RGB [0, 255], and write a compressed PNG. The sphere is not displaced.

assets.license_note: NASA content generally is not subject to copyright in the United States and is subject to NASA's Images and Media Usage Guidelines. The normal map is a project-generated derivative. Credit NASA/GSFC/SVS and the LRO LOLA team; attribution does not imply endorsement.

channel.semantics: Project-generated shading normals derived from quantitative NASA LOLA displacement data. Slope is visually amplified 48x; values are not elevation, do not displace geometry, and are not unmodified NASA data.

source.organization: NASA Planetary Data System Geosciences Node; Mars Global Surveyor Mars Orbiter Laser Altimeter team
source.title: MOLA Mission Experiment Gridded Data Record, global topography, 16 pixels per degree
source.label: https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/mgs/urn-nasa-pds-mgs_mola_topography_derived/meg016/megt90n000eb.xml
source.data_semantics: Big-endian signed 16-bit global topography in metres above the MOLA areoid; equirectangular, positive-east, 0 to 360 degrees longitude, centered at 180 degrees.

transforms: Read the 5760 x 2880 detached-label raster as big-endian signed 16-bit metre values and bilinearly resample it to 2048 x 1024.
Roll sampling by 180 degrees (half the source width) so the source 0 to 360 degree longitude domain aligns with the runtime -180 to 180 degree color map.
Compute central height differences with longitude wrap, clamped polar rows, and latitude-aware east-west metre spacing using a 3,396,190 m radius.
Multiply physical surface slopes by 1.4 for visual legibility, normalize the tangent-space vector, encode XYZ from [-1, 1] to RGB [0, 255], and write a compressed PNG. The sphere is not displaced.

assets.license_note: NASA/PDS data generally is not subject to copyright in the United States and is subject to NASA's media-use guidance and the archive citation instructions. The normal map is a project-generated derivative. Credit NASA PDS, MGS, and the MOLA team; attribution does not imply endorsement.

channel.semantics: Project-generated shading normals derived from quantitative NASA MOLA topography. Slope is visually amplified 1.4x; values are not elevation, do not displace geometry, and are not unmodified NASA data.

source.organization: NASA Earth Observatory / Goddard Space Flight Center
source.title: Blue Marble: Next Generation with Topography, August, 8192 x 4096 runtime reduction
source.data_semantics: Static color visualization with compositing and GTOPO30-style shaded relief already present; not quantitative elevation.

transforms: Evaluate Rec. 601-style luminance (0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B) directly from normalized 8-bit Blue Marble code values.
Use wrapped central image-luminance differences, attenuated by the square of one minus the separately derived ocean mask and a 1.7 visual factor, to create a low-strength relief cue.
Normalize the tangent-space vector, encode XYZ from [-1, 1] to RGB [0, 255], and write a compressed 2048 x 1024 PNG. No quantitative height is inferred and the sphere is not displaced.

assets.license_note: NASA content generally is not subject to copyright in the United States and is subject to NASA's Images and Media Usage Guidelines. This relief proxy is a project-generated heuristic derivative. Credit NASA/GSFC and Blue Marble's stated contributors; attribution does not imply endorsement.

channel.semantics: Project-authored image-relief proxy derived from Blue Marble luminance. It is not DEM-derived, measured topography, or a scientific normal product.

source.organization: NASA Earth Observatory / Goddard Space Flight Center
source.title: Blue Marble: Next Generation with Topography, August, 8192 x 4096 runtime reduction
source.data_semantics: Static color visualization; it contains no authoritative land-water classification channel.

transforms: For normalized 8-bit Blue Marble code values, compute blue dominance as B - 0.72 * max(R, G).
Map blue dominance through smoothstep edges 0.035 and 0.19 and write the result as an 8-bit grayscale 2048 x 1024 PNG, where 0 is land-like and 255 is water-like.

assets.license_note: NASA content generally is not subject to copyright in the United States and is subject to NASA's Images and Media Usage Guidelines. This mask is a project-generated heuristic derivative. Credit NASA/GSFC and Blue Marble's stated contributors; attribution does not imply endorsement.

channel.semantics: Project-authored blue-dominance confidence mask used for ocean glint. It is not an authoritative coastline, water mask, bathymetry, ice mask, or sea-state dataset.

source.organization: NASA Earth Observatory / Goddard Space Flight Center
source.title: Blue Marble: Next Generation with Topography, August, 8192 x 4096 runtime reduction
source.data_semantics: Static color visualization; it contains no measured PBR roughness channel.

transforms: Compute Rec. 601-style luminance and the project-derived blue-dominance ocean mask from normalized 8-bit Blue Marble code values.
Set land-like roughness to clamp(0.68 + (0.5 - luminance) * 0.18, 0.55, 0.86), blend toward 0.12 by the ocean-mask value, and encode the result as an 8-bit grayscale 2048 x 1024 PNG.

source.organization: Space Telescope Science Institute Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes; NASA/ESA Hubble Outer Planet Atmospheres Legacy program
source.title: OPAL Saturn Cycle 32 Rotation A color global map, F395N/F502N/F631N

transforms: Downloaded the official OPAL TIFF byte-for-byte from MAST.
Preserved the 1800 x 900 equirectangular projection and source composite color without cropping, resizing, or reprojection.

Encoded per-pixel coverage alpha with a smoothstep from source luma 24 to 72 so black no-data polar rows and the ring-obscured equatorial strip fall back to the continuous procedural atmosphere at runtime.

Clamped isolated source channels to plus or minus 18 code values around each valid row median to suppress transiting moons, moon shadows, and mosaic outliers disclosed by the OPAL readme, then encoded 8-bit RGBA pixels as lossless WebP with scripts/generate-phase5-saturn-map.mjs.
Runtime blends the observed sample at up to 86 percent strength over the project-authored Cassini-wind-driven layer; source gaps remain procedural and no missing coverage is fabricated.
assets.license_note: Credit NASA, ESA, STScI, and the Hubble OPAL team. NASA content generally is not subject to copyright in the United States and remains subject to NASA and MAST media/data policies; attribution does not imply endorsement.

color_space.runtime: sRGB color with linear coverage alpha

projection.type: OPAL equirectangular global map at 5 pixels per degree
projection.latitude: full 180-degree raster; no-data polar and ring-obscured rows carry reduced or zero alpha and fall back to procedural haze
projection.longitude: full 360-degree System III west-longitude coverage, decreasing to the right

channel.semantics: Dated Hubble WFC3/UVIS color composite mosaicked from Rotation A observations acquired 2025-08-29. It is a cloud-color foundation with disclosed coverage cleanup, not measured albedo, live Saturnian weather, or a reconstruction at the selected simulation date.

source.organization: NASA/JPL-Caltech/SwRI/MSSS; image processing by Kevin M. Gill
source.title: The Great Red Spot, PIA23606 enhanced-color JunoCam mosaic

transforms: Downloaded the official PIA23606 TIFF byte-for-byte from NASA Science.

Cropped source pixels x=1450..2792 and y=80..1129, extended the right and lower edges only outside the used inner-vortex sample footprint, and preserved the crop center as the shader's local vortex center.
Converted the crop to grayscale, applied sigma 0.55 denoising and a sigma 16 low-pass, then encoded 128 + 1.65 * (fine - low-pass) as a neutral-centered 1600 x 1130 luminance-residual map.

Encoded the one-channel residual as lossless WebP. PIA23606 enhanced color is not imported; runtime blends only restrained luminance detail over dated Hubble OPAL color and sampled cloud structure inside an authored elliptical mask.

projection.type: project-fitted local elliptical detail coordinates; not a calibrated planetary map projection
projection.coverage: inner Great Red Spot only; surrounding OPAL pixels remain authoritative, while the moving storm boundary is an authored elliptical blend informed by cited approximate dimensions

channel.semantics: Illustrative multi-epoch enhancement from a February 12, 2019 JunoCam mosaic, blended over the December 11, 2025 Hubble OPAL map. It is not a calibrated 2025 reconstruction, measured wind field, forecast, or live-weather product.
